events.text: Constellation Software announced a binding agreement to acquire 100% of Total Specific Solutions (TSS) B.V., a Netherlands-based group (Everest, Blueriq, KZA, PharmaPartners, PinkRoccade Local Government, PinkRoccade Healthcare, Yonde), for approximately EUR 240 million before representations-and-warranties adjustments, then the company's largest deal. TSS had annual gross revenue of approximately EUR 174 million and about 1,400 employees. Constellation added a one-year US$350 million term loan to fund the deal.

events.item: President's letter: hurdle rates and acquisition pace
events.text: Third-party analyses of Mark Leonard's shareholder/president's letters (covering years including part of this window) describe hurdle rates as 'magnetic' (pulling down expected IRRs across all pursued opportunities when lowered) and describe a long-run ambition to expand acquisition capacity from about 40 per year toward 100 per year. These are third-party syntheses of the letters, not direct quotes tied to a specific year's letter within FY2012-2016; the exact letter text and year-by-year hurdle-rate or acquisition-count statements were not confirmed within the search budget.

events.item: President's letter 2015: organic growth vs. IRR, reason for buying shrinking businesses
events.text: SECOND PASS: third-party summaries of the 2015 president's/shareholder letter describe Leonard analyzing Constellation's own acquisition data and concluding there is 'little correlation' between a business's post-acquisition organic growth rate and the investment return (IRR) it generates -- Constellation's best and worst-performing acquisitions have come from businesses across the organic growth spectrum. The stated implication is that Constellation is willing to buy shrinking businesses provided the price is right and projected IRR clears the hurdle rate, deliberately not screening out targets on organic growth alone. This is offered as context for why reported organic growth turned negative in 2015 (the company was not avoiding low/negative-organic-growth targets), but no direct quote from the original 2015 letter was recovered, and the letter's own explicit explanation for the FY2015 organic growth figure specifically (-3% reported / +3% FX-adjusted) was not located verbatim within the search budget.
events.source_title: Business Lessons from Mark Leonard (Constellation Software) - 25iq (third-party synthesis)

events.text: SECOND PASS: Constellation's 2013 President's Letter to Shareholders states 'Organic Net Revenue Growth was 4% in 2013' and, per a separate summary of the same letter, that 'Total Organic Growth in Maintenance Revenue was 8% in 2013, a slight increase from 2012' -- two distinct organic growth metrics (total revenue vs. maintenance revenue specifically) both stated for FY2013.
